by: Kar (Claude Opus 5.5), the builder, simulating four buyers
how: The served page (HTTP 200, the build at commit 9279910) read cold from the top in a browser with its scripts run, as each buyer in turn: every section, button and number. Then the COO followed How you make passports on your own machine step by step on a made-up notes folder. Each gap was answered from the repository's own code, records and sealed claims, or is listed as open.

gaps.gap: The role cards were titled Finance and Operations, so a CFO or COO had to guess which card was theirs.
gaps.answered: For your business: the cards are CEO or owner, CFO and finance, COO and operations, CTO / CISO, Procurement and the teams.

gaps.gap: The cost case assumes a team can make passports from its own notes, and the page's steps gave no way to do that (the COO's gaps below).
gaps.answered: How you make passports on your own machine: the notes command, run as written on every push (claims-notes.json N1).

gaps.gap: The case for the board says every claim is re-checked by an open test anyone can run, and the page never said how to run it.
gaps.answered: The proof, Check the proof yourself: the commands, with each receipt re-derived on your own machine.

gaps.gap: The G3 FAILED row lists its matches as file, kind and line, with no plain reading of what they are.
gaps.answered: The proof, The failures in plain words: each kind of match counted from the receipt and read; a page test fails if a kind has no reading.

gaps.gap: The blueprint said the codec was compared on a thousand tokens; the receipt gives the exact count.
gaps.answered: Blueprint, The codec: the count is read from the receipt (P2 and P3).

gaps.gap: The page says nothing is baselined, and the CI file enforced that only on the time case's gate.
gaps.answered: CI: every organ's gate now fails the build on a baselined survivor.

gaps.gap: Following How you make passports on your own machine, verify refused my own passports: the clone trusts Kar's pinned public key, and the steps never said to pin your own.
gaps.answered: Step 3: node kar/passport.mjs key > keys/kar.json makes your key and pins it. The key's own note and the hand-back's refusal no longer say Kar.

gaps.gap: With every step followed, none of the notes reached any slice, not even the full one: the slicer reads Kar's own memory (its digest, its working memory and the sections of its index), so the roll-out's week 1 could not be done.
gaps.answered: A new organ, src/notes.mjs, and the notes command, sealed in claims-notes.json before the code: N1, the steps run as written on a made-up team's notes in a fresh copy of the repository, and N2, the organ witness-clean. Both re-derived in CI.

gaps.gap: What must our notes look like?
gaps.answered: How you make passports on your own machine, What your notes look like: the layout Claude Code's memory folder uses, and the two optional lines.

gaps.gap: No card for procurement among the roles.

gaps.answered: Security, Sub-processors: none of ours; the only processor is the AI you paste into.
